YoY, these imports rose +151%, the largest YoY increase on record, compared with peak annual growth of just +34% during the 2000 Dot-Com Boom.

Based on September's figures, these imports are now running at an annualized rate above $1.0 trillion for the first time.

US demand for technology hardware is exploding.

BREAKING: Global crude oil in transit is up to 1.28 billion barrels, an all-time high.

This figure has surged +180 million barrels over the last several weeks.

This comes as Middle Eastern oil flows recover through the Strait of Hormuz and alternative routes, while more crude remains at sea for longer.

Ship-to-ship transfers are keeping oil aboard tankers for longer, while extended shipping routes are increasing transit times.

Meanwhile, global oil importers diversifying away from the Middle East are lengthening voyages, leaving more crude tied up aboard tankers.

As a result, more oil remains in transit rather than being readily available to refiners, tightening near-term supply despite recovering export flows.

Oil is flowing, but timely delivery is becoming the bottleneck.

BREAKING: US job openings jumped +333,000 in September, to 7.52 million, the 3rd-highest reading since November 2024.

This marks the largest monthly increase since April and the 3rd-largestsince October 2024.

The surge was led by professional and business services, which added +106,000 openings.

State and local government, excluding education, followed, with an increase of +104,000.

As a result, the ratio of job openings to unemployed workers rose to 1.06, its highest since January 2025.

There are now 414,000 more available vacancies than unemployed workers, the 2nd-largest difference since January 2025.

US labor demand appears to be recovering.

The US momentum trade is facing a historic unwind:

This also marks its 3rd-largest daily decline since its inception in April 2013.

$MTUM has dropped -16% over the last 5 trading sessions, to its lowest level since April 7th.

From its June peak, the fund is now down -27%, even exceeding the February-April 2025 drawdown of -25%.

This follows a +38% gain from the beginning of 2026 to its June 22nd peak.

The momentum trade is experiencing historic volatility.

US semiconductor stocks have rarely been this volatile:

The Semiconductor Index, SOX, has declined -21.8% over the last 5 trading sessions, its largest 5-day decline since September 21st, 2001, following the Dot-Com Bubble burst.

Not even 2008 or 2020 saw such large 5-day drawdowns.

The ETF's largest 5-day decline was recorded on April 14th, 2000, at -27.1%.

On Thursday alone, SOX fell -12.3%, its largest 1-day decline since March 16th, 2020, when the index fell -15.9%.

Meanwhile, the 3x leveraged long semiconductor ETF, SOXL, has fallen -60% over the last 5 trading sessions, and is down -86% from its June peak.

We don't know in advance if the breakout will succeed or fail. This is making peace with uncertainty. I know many would like to have some kind of certainty in the business of trading. It doesn't exist. 

Confirm the breakout, place the stop below the pattern boundary, place at the market sell order at the price target (incase a sharp move takes place to the target) and avoid overriding these decisions (unless dictated by predetermined rules).

As momentum/breakout traders we need to be indifferent on the possible direction of the price action. 

We need as much as possible uninterrupted directional movement. Choppy markets are where the breakout strategy struggles. 

This rectangle could have broken on the upside, the way to take advantage of the directional move would have been the same.

Global Equity Markets report started featuring some short setups lately. As markets establish their trends below the long-term averages, I will focus more on the short side. 

This doesn't mean either long or short setups. We are being very selective and only if the pattern is clearly horizontal with well-defined boundaries. 

I am not predicting a crash or bear market. I just want to take advantage of any fast moving directional move to capture Type 1 and Type 2 breakouts.
